statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail 17% sits in the low band and Stress 44% is moderate, with the BOJ decision already printed and absorbed.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. The BOJ hike has printed and was absorbed without one-way continuation, so conditional risk is concentrated in two narrow windows rather than across the whole session: the 06:30Z Ueda press conference and the 13:30Z US cash open on quadruple-witching expiry. Outside those windows the observed overnight structure remains two-way and Tail stays below the block threshold.
headline: NAS100 holds a narrow overnight range near 29,520 after an orderly BOJ hike; Ueda press conference and quad-witching expiry frame the day's risk windows
body: Nasdaq-100 cash closed Thursday near 29,447, up 1.73% (+501.92 points), in a broad relief rally that followed Wednesday's 25bp Federal Reserve hike to 3.75-4.00%, the first US increase in more than three years; the Nasdaq Composite rose 1.69% to 26,418.30 and the S&P 500 1.14% to 7,637.77, with VIX down 12.8% to 15.44. The Bank of Japan then raised its policy rate 25bp to 1.25% in the Asian session, the highest in 31 years and its first hike since June. That print was absorbed without a yen-carry shock: the Nikkei 225 rose 1.67% to 65,208 after the decision and NAS100 trades near 29,522, about +0.25% overnight, having recovered off the overnight low, so meaningful retracement remains available and structure is two-way. Cross-asset signals are not aligned for a one-way equity path: 2-year and 10-year Treasury yields are only marginally higher at 4.70% and 4.95% after Thursday's decline, VIX is low, and crude is easing for a third session near $100.95 WTI and $103.69 Brent as Saudi Arabia restores East-West pipeline capacity damaged by drone attacks last week. Tail is therefore held at 17% in the low band. Stress is 44% because two independent catalysts remain ahead: Governor Ueda's 06:30Z press conference, the delayed second leg of the BOJ decision and the main yen-carry transmission channel, and the 13:30Z US cash open, where Fed Governor Bowman and the expiry-day opening rotation land on the same instant into an already bullish regime. The September quadruple-witching settles at the 20:00Z cash close. CME index futures then halt for the weekend from 21:00Z, which removes any live price path and lowers both conditional Tail and Confidence across the final eight forecast hours.

lookbackSummary: Over the past 24 hours Tail ranged 17-26% and Stress decayed from 66% to 41% as the post-Fed relief rally matured. The single orange hour was 13:00Z Thursday, at the US cash open, when trend-up structure was most pronounced. Tail fell back through the afternoon as retracements reappeared, and the overnight hours settled into a normal, range-bound mode with Tail 17-18% and Confidence steady near 87%, with Stress ticking back up at 04:00Z as the BOJ decision approached.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours carry two narrow conditional-risk peaks. Tail rises into the watch band around the 06:30Z Ueda press conference, peaking at 22% at 07:00Z where the Q&A overlaps the European cash open, then eases through the European morning. The single hour mapped to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES is 14:00Z, covering the first 30-90 minutes after the expiry-day cash open, where Tail is 25% and falls back if the opening auction shows normal-depth retracement. A secondary Stress peak accompanies the 20:00Z quadruple-witching settlement. From 21:00Z the CME weekend halt removes any live price path, so Tail falls to 13-15% and Confidence eases into the solid band.
